items.q: A 35-year-old patient with a chronic scaphoid proximal pole non-union is found to have no punctate bleeding from the proximal fragment during surgery. MRI shows evidence of avascular necrosis. Which of the following is the most appropriate surgical treatment?
o: Matti-Russe volar inlay cancellous bone graft
items.e: Proximal pole non-union with AVN (confirmed by lack of punctate bleeding) requires a vascularized bone graft. The 1,2-ICSRA (Zaidemberg) graft is the most common pedicled option; non-vascularized grafts like the Matti-Russe have high failure rates in this setting.
items.note: Refined the stem to be more direct and improved the explanation to clarify why vascularized grafts are preferred over non-vascularized options in AVN.

items.q: In the mechanics of the proximal carpal row, the lunate acts as an intercalated segment. Which of the following statements correctly describes the inherent rotational tendencies of the adjacent bones?
o: The scaphoid tends to extend and the triquetrum tends to flex
The scaphoid tends to flex and the triquetrum tends to extend
Both the scaphoid and triquetrum tend to flex
Both the scaphoid and triquetrum tend to extend
items.e: The scaphoid has an inherent tendency to flex, while the triquetrum has an inherent tendency to extend. The lunate is balanced between these opposing forces by the scapholunate and lunotriquetral ligaments.
items.note: Fundamental carpal kinematics fact.

items.q: A respiratory therapist presents with clustered clear vesicles on an erythematous base on the tip of her thumb. She reports a prodrome of tingling and intense pain. Which of the following is absolutely contraindicated in the management of this patient?
items.e: This is a herpetic whitlow (HSV infection). Incision and drainage are contraindicated because they can lead to secondary bacterial infection and potentially systemic viraemia, including encephalitis. Management is primarily non-operative and self-limiting.
items.note: The clinical presentation is classic for herpetic whitlow, and the contraindication of I&D is a high-yield exam fact.

items.q: According to Kanavel's criteria for pyogenic flexor tenosynovitis, which of the following clinical findings is recognized as the earliest and most sensitive sign of the infection?
o: The finger is held in a position of semi-flexion
Symmetrical (fusiform) swelling of the entire digit
Tenderness localized along the course of the flexor sheath
Pain on passive extension of the digit
items.e: While all four are Kanavel's signs, pain on passive extension is the earliest and most sensitive sign of pyogenic flexor tenosynovitis, indicating irritation within the synovial sheath.
items.note: This is a standard orthopaedic fact regarding the sensitivity of Kanavel's signs.
items.reason: Duplicates ai20261115_009 idea; 'earliest sign' is contested

items.q: A 40-year-old manual labourer presents with a 'collar-button' (web space) abscess. On examination, the adjacent fingers are abducted and there is significant swelling on both the volar and dorsal aspects of the web. What is the correct surgical approach for drainage?
o: Single transverse incision across the palmar web
High lateral mid-axial incision on the adjacent finger
items.e: A collar-button abscess is a dumbbell-shaped infection with volar and dorsal components connected through the palmar fascia. Drainage requires dual incisions (volar and dorsal) to address both compartments; incisions should never cross the web space itself to avoid contracture.
items.note: The question correctly identifies the dumbbell nature of the abscess and the standard dual-incision approach.

items.q: When evaluating a patient for suspected necrotising fasciitis of the upper limb, which of the following laboratory parameters is NOT a component of the LRINEC (Laboratory Risk Indicator for Necrotising Fasciitis) score?
items.e: The LRINEC score includes CRP, White Blood Cell count, Haemoglobin, Sodium, Creatinine, and Glucose. ESR is not a component of this scoring system.
items.note: The LRINEC score is a standard clinical tool for necrotising fasciitis, and knowing its components is essential for postgraduate exams.

items.q: A 22-year-old painter sustains a high-pressure injection injury to his non-dominant index finger with an oil-based solvent. Despite an innocuous-looking entry wound, he is at significant risk. What is the reported amputation rate for oil-based paint injections?
items.e: Oil-based paints and solvents cause severe chemical inflammation and tissue necrosis, leading to amputation rates as high as 50-60%. These injuries are surgical emergencies requiring wide debridement, ideally within 6 hours.
items.note: The question highlights the severity and specific prognosis of oil-based high-pressure injection injuries as documented in Campbell's.
